planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring into acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this southern Appalachian native naturally colonizes dry rocky slopes, heath balds, and bog margins at higher elevations and resents heavy, poorly drained clay.

directions: Mountain fetterbush is a twiggy, arching deciduous shrub that produces one-sided racemes of small white urn-shaped flowers along bare, reddish stems just before the leaves emerge in spring. In the wild it colonizes acidic, rocky, high-elevation slopes and heath balds of the southern Appalachians, so a woodland garden with dappled light and a leaf-litter mulch suits it far better than a tidy foundation bed. Its loosely rounded, suckering habit makes it more useful for naturalizing a shady bank or native plant collection than for formal hedging. Fall foliage turns a respectable red, after which the shrub's wiry red-brown winter twigs carry the seasonal interest.
sources: North Carolina State University Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into lean, acidic, excessively well-drained sandy soil in full sun, mimicking the exposed Atlantic dune systems of Portugal and Galicia where this species grows wild; it is dioecious, so both a male and female plant are needed for fruit.

directions: White crowberry is a low, mounding, heath-like evergreen shrub from the sand dunes of the Iberian Atlantic coast, with needle-fine foliage and a wiry, wind-sculpted habit well suited to sandy, salt-exposed sites. Small pink flowers appear in late winter to early spring, followed by clusters of white, berry-like drupes that ripen in early summer and have long been gathered locally for traditional preserves and refreshing drinks. Because it is dioecious, plant several seedlings or propagate from both male and female stock to guarantee fruit set. Give it lean, acidic, extremely fast-draining sand and avoid any supplemental feeding, since rich soil and standing moisture quickly weaken this drought-adapted dune specialist.
sources: Rediscovering Portuguese White Crowberries (Corema album): Cultural Insights and Nutritional Significance, PMC
Corema album (L.) D.Don, the white crowberry — a new crop (ResearchGate)

planting.note: Plant balled-and-burlapped or container stock in spring in deep, consistently moist, well-drained soil in full sun; give this fast-growing walnut relative plenty of room, since it suckers from the base and develops a broad, rounded crown.

directions: Caucasian wingnut is a vigorous, fast-growing relative of walnut and hickory, native from the Caucasus to northern Iran, grown for its handsome compound leaves bearing up to two dozen glossy leaflets and its long, pendulous strings of small winged nutlets that dangle like green tassels through summer into fall. It tolerates compacted, heavy soils far better than most large shade trees and shrugs off occasional drought once established, though it grows fastest and largest along stream banks and other reliably moist sites. Because mature specimens can exceed sixty feet with an equally wide crown and a tendency to sucker from the base, reserve it for parks, large estates, or other sites where its eventual scale and root spread will not conflict with buildings or pavement. Its early-season pollen-shedding catkins also make it a useful, if under-recognized, source of nectar and pollen for early-flying bees.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped stock in spring in moist to wet, well-drained soil in full sun; this riverbank native from central and eastern China is an excellent choice beside a pond or stream and tolerates clay and seasonal flooding that would stress most shade trees.

directions: Chinese wingnut is a fast-growing, wide-crowned shade tree distinguished from its close relatives by a narrow, serrated wing running along the central leaf rachis between the leaflets. Native to riverbanks and moist alpine forests of China, it tolerates wet, compacted, and clay soils that few other large trees can handle, making it a practical choice for low-lying or occasionally flooded ground beside a pond or stream. In summer the tree produces long, pendulous catkins that mature into strings of small winged nutlets, adding texture through the growing season before dropping in fall. Once established it also tolerates considerable drought and wind, but it grows largest and fastest with reliable moisture and full sun.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension, ENH-691/ST533: Pterocarya stenoptera
Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)
Van den Berk Nurseries Tree Guide

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in a sheltered site with deep, consistently moist, well-drained soil in full to partial sun; this subtropical Chinese walnut relative is still rare in cultivation outside specialty collections and benefits from wind protection while young.

directions: Wheel wingnut is a broad-crowned, pinnate-leaved relative of the walnuts native to warm-temperate forests of central and southern China, grown both for its ornamental golden-yellow fall color and for its distinctive flattened, disc-shaped winged nuts that give the tree its common name. It is still uncommon outside botanical and specialty tree collections in the West, so sourcing nursery-grown stock can take some searching, but mature trees reward patience with a graceful, wide-spreading canopy. It prefers a humid, warm-summer climate with deep, evenly moist, well-drained soil and appreciates shelter from strong wind while the trunk and branch structure are developing. In its native range the dried leaves are also valued for a traditional herbal tea, adding a secondary use beyond its role as a specimen shade tree.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean's Trees and Shrubs)
Research Progress and Sustainable Use of Cyclocarya paliurus (Juglandaceae), ResearchGate

planting.note: Plant bulb offsets or container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; this Mexican oak-woodland native begins active growth with the onset of warm-season rain, so avoid overwatering during its dry dormant period.

directions: Mexican firecracker forms a basal rosette of glossy, narrow, grass-like leaves from a fleshy rootstock, sending up slender flower spikes bearing distinctive paired, tubular, coral-orange to reddish flowers from midsummer into fall. Native to winter-dry oak woodlands in Mexico, it greens up and flowers in response to the onset of warm-season rain, so irrigation should taper off during its cooler dry-season dormancy to avoid rot. The tubular flowers are a strong hummingbird draw late in the season when fewer other nectar sources are in bloom. Grow it in well-drained soil in a xeric or rock garden border, where its narrow foliage and vivid paired blooms make a useful textural contrast to broader-leaved companions.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery — Polianthes geminiflora 'Colima Form'
